question: Does finite-time propagation of chaos or mean-field stability hold uniformly for all t under only smooth globally Lipschitz deterministic Vlasov interactions and finite first moments?

scope.model: One-dimensional Vlasov equation with K(r)=r^2/2, force K'(x-y)=x-y, and its N-particle empirical system.
scope.initial_data: For every N, iid Z_i(0)~Normal(0,I_2), with position and velocity independent.
scope.metric: Phase-space W1 with cost |x-y|+|v-w|; position-marginal W1 gives a lower bound by projection.
scope.quantifier: The result is a counterexample to a universal theorem over the stated deterministic class, not over dissipative or stochastic subclasses.

claims.statement: For fixed T<infinity, the tagged position marginal rho^N_{1,t} is O_T(N^-1) close in W1 to the Vlasov position marginal rho_t, uniformly for 0<=t<=T.
claims.evidence: q(t)=cosh(2t), q_N(t)=(1-1/N)cosh(2t)+(1+t^2)/N; W1=sqrt(2/pi)(sqrt(q)-sqrt(q_N)) and is bounded by sqrt(2/pi)cosh(2T)/N.

claims.statement: At t_N=log(N)+c, for each fixed real c, W1(rho^N_{1,t_N},rho_{t_N}) tends to exp(c)/(2sqrt(pi)); hence uniform-in-time tagged chaos in W1 fails.
claims.evidence: At t_N, q/N^2->exp(2c)/2 and (q-q_N)/N->exp(2c)/2; rationalizing square roots yields the limit.

claims.statement: For each finite N the tagged position W1 error diverges as t->infinity, asymptotic to exp(t)/sqrt(pi)*(1-sqrt(1-1/N)).
The Vlasov solution map has no time-independent W1 Lipschitz stability constant on centered Gaussian initial laws near Normal(0,I_2).
claims.evidence: Scale data by a; position W1 at time t is sqrt(2/pi)|a-1|sqrt(cosh(2t)), while initial phase W1<=2sqrt(2/pi)|a-1|. The ratio is >=0.5sqrt(cosh(2t))~exp(t)/(2sqrt(2)).

claims.statement: A primary-source W1 stability theorem provides finite-time control for this model but does not give a uniform-in-time factor.
claims.evidence: Iacobelli 2022 states the directly applicable classical Dobrushin estimate W1(f1(t),f2(t))<=exp[(1+2B)t]W1(f1(0),f2(0)); for this R model B=1, so the factor is exp(3t). Its refined Theorem 2.1 is recorded separately because its displayed proof uses the torus.

claims.statement: Uniform-in-time chaos theorems for dissipative stochastic kinetic models do not contradict this deterministic unstable counterexample.
claims.evidence: Monmarche 2017 treats a Vlasov-Fokker-Planck/Langevin system with friction, noise, strictly convex external confinement, and a semiconvex interaction under Assumption 1.

model_equations.vlasov: partial_t f+v partial_x f+(x-m_x[f_t]) partial_v f=0

costs.source_acquisition: Bounded web pass over three primary research sources; no dataset or corpus download.
costs.derivation: Closed-form scalar mode solution and Gaussian covariance algebra; no simulation or numerical ODE.
costs.precision: Exact symbolic formulas; no floating-point arithmetic or tolerance.
costs.formal_verification: Not checked in a proof assistant; independent review should rederive the center/residual variance decomposition and the t=log N+c limit.

falsifier: An independent recomputation showing the center/relative modes or q_N(t) differ from the formulas; or a purported theorem with exactly this deterministic system, datum, tagged marginal, fixed W1 norm, and all-time quantifiers (which would force an audit of an assumption mismatch).

primary_sources.author: R. L. Dobrushin
primary_sources.title: Vlasov equations
primary_sources.used_for: Original Vlasov mean-field framework, existence/uniqueness, and finite-time weak convergence.

primary_sources.author: Mikaela Iacobelli
primary_sources.title: A New Perspective on Wasserstein Distances for Kinetic Problems
primary_sources.used_for: General-domain W1 definitions and the classical Dobrushin stability estimate; Theorem 2.1 refined factor is recorded with a domain caveat.

primary_sources.author: Pierre Monmarche
primary_sources.title: Long-time behaviour and propagation of chaos for mean field kinetic particles
primary_sources.used_for: Positive uniform-in-time result for a different, damped/noisy, strictly confined kinetic model.
